candidate_facts.text: The Korean War concluded with an armistice signed on July 27, 1953.
The armistice that ended the Korean War is not a peace treaty but a truce.
The conflict remains technically ongoing because no formal peace treaty was ever signed.
The fighting in the Korean War ended in a stalemate with no clear winner or loser.
The armistice restored the boundary along the 38th parallel.
The armistice established the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).
The DMZ was set as a 2.5-mile-wide fortified buffer.
